portion_doctrine: Segments 71-80 are a collection of design/fashion interview transcripts (John Galliano at Maison Margiela + Schiaparelli) plus AI-design-process conversations. Heavy on timestamps and UI boilerplate; real content extracted below.
operating_rules: Include collaborators from the beginning of the creative process, give them space to research and iterate
Drip-feed successful techniques from experimental 'Artisano' collection down to commercial ready-to-wear lines for affordability
Listen to fabric properties - they dictate how they want to be cut, draped, handled
Silhouette/corsetry creates the structural foundation - everything that comes after must fit the waist/hip measurements
Emphasize the behind-the-scenes process and ethics of craft to justify the luxury price; communicate that clothes have soul, not just production
Maintain discipline of traditional dress-making construction (the 'scaffolding') before decorating
Use obsessions (3-4 per day minimum) as the heartbeat that pulls you through the design process
Build collections from found objects and research; let one object seed entire collection directions
Embroidery placement on grain vs bias: cuts from iris (bias), embroiders on the straight of grain for stability without pulling
AI is a tool for process efficiency, not design replacement; human hands, pattern-making, and creative decision-making remain non-negotiable
Traditional design process (research-discovery-ideate) is changing; don't trust it as gospel
named_methods: Artisano collection model: small, experimental line that feeds successful techniques into commercial collections
Objects-as-seeders: surround yourself with found objects that spark story ideas for collections
Couture-to-ready-to-wear translation: develop solutions in haute couture first, then find industrial/affordable versions for mass production
Bias-cutting technique with modern embroidery research: use closeup photography and modern tech to reverse-engineer historical techniques
Dialogue with fabric: listen to material properties to determine construction methods
Pattern-making with tech design: tech design is job security in AI era (sourcing, pattern-making, construction knowledge)
numbers: Fewer and fewer couture houses globally (declining count mentioned)
Multiple processes in one step (modern equipment capability)
specific_tactics: Develop waist/hip measurements as the anchor constraint for silhouettes, forcing fit over all ornament
Use closeup photography and modern tech to study historical embroidery placement and reverse-engineer technique
Collaborate with specialized suppliers (embroiderers, fabric houses, specialists) to maintain craft quality
Keep suppliers busy and bring in new talent to maintain ecosystem health
Show behind-the-scenes making process to communicate craftsmanship and soul, not just aesthetic
Objects sharing ritual: gather objects that inspire team members, use them to unlock collection stories
Dress for wearability first (where body moves) then maximize ornament in static zones
tools: Modern technology for studying historical techniques
AI design tools (contextual use for efficiency, not decision-making)
skills: Research and reverse-engineering from historical garments
Collaboration and delegation with creative autonomy
gates: Market dates and show deadlines cannot shift (commercial reality gate)
Fabric properties dictate construction method (material reality gate)
Silhouette fit must honor body measurements before ornament (engineering gate)
Collaborators must be included at ideation start, not added mid-process
content_ideas: Object-to-collection case studies (umbrella collection, object-inspired designs)
Craft vs AI positioning in luxury fashion
Supplier/embroiderer spotlight and sustainability in craft
Structured interview format with designers on creative obsessions
contradictions: Push for experimental couture innovation vs. commercial ready-to-wear constraints
AI efficiency tools are valuable but cannot replace human creative decision-making (nuanced, not binary)
Embrace surprise collaborations and unplanned ideas vs. structured market schedule discipline
weird_gold: Vionnet embroiders on the straight of grain, not bias - discovered via modern closeup photography in 2024 that was never documented
Bias-cut fabric will naturally pull embroidery unless grain placement is correct
Designers taught to trust traditional design process (research-discovery-ideate) but that process itself is now obsolete
Obsessions (multiple per day) are the actual fuel/heartbeat of collections, not careful planning
Fabric speaks if you listen - it tells you how it wants to be handled
